content.thinking:
I'm planning the full file structure, importing the builder and helper modules I'll need, then sketching out proportions for a qilin creature at roughly shoulder height of 1.6 meters.

Now I'm working out the geometry: sweeping the spine from rump to chest with a tapering radius, building the neck and head with a dragon-like muzzle, then adding four deer-style legs with capsule segments down to hoof cylinders planted at y=0. For the coat, I'm applying a cel-shaded scales paint in teal tones over the body surface.

For color design, I'm settling on an anime-style qilin look: pearl-white scaled body shaded teal, with a cream belly region split by a normal-based paint condition, gold antlers and hooves, a swirling teal-gold cloud mane and tail rendered as textured cards, glowing eyes and forehead gem, plus small flame-wisp accents on the fetlocks.

I'm figuring out the mane construction by scattering cloud puffs and cards along the neck, manually walking a catmull path with a for loop since I'm unsure of the built-in "along" signature, and using sphere parts clustered together for the cloud puffs alongside cards for the swirl shapes. For the head and eyes, I'm placing a sphere part for the head and adding eye decals onto its surface using the hit/stick system.

Now I'm laying out the head geometry: setting a skull center point with a scaled sphere, building a tapered rod for the muzzle, and positioning eye decals on the skull surface at calculated azimuth/elevation angles so they land on the front-side of the head without colliding with the muzzle. I'm also planning small dark spheres for nostrils, long thin gold catmull sweeps for whiskers, and spike shapes for a beard tuft under the chin.

For the antlers, I'm writing a helper function that builds a branching catmull path starting at the skull top and curving upward and backward, with tapering radius values, mirrored for left and right sides using a sign multiplier.

I'm continuing to flesh out the antler helper with branch spikes sprouting from points along the main path and glowing teal spheres capping the tips, then moving to ear geometry using flattened spike cones angled outward and backward from the skull, and finally sketching an SVG wisp shape for body hair cards that can be tinted by color.

Now I'm filtering which card frames belong on the mane versus tail based on surface normal direction, using the hit normal's y and x components to isolate the back-of-neck region where the mane should scatter.

For the mane puffs, I'm sampling points along a curve from chest to head base and offsetting each point backward and upward to place cloud-like sphere clusters there, coloring them in alternating teal, cream, white, and aqua tones, with small torus swirls mixed in for texture.

Now I'm adding decorative cloud-swirl decals on the flanks using a gold-teal spiral SVG pattern applied via decal mapping, positioning them symmetrically on either side of the body with a spiral path drawn in the SVG.

Next I'm shaping the tail as a lion-like curved sweep from the rump upward and back using a tapered radius, finishing with cloud-tuft puffs at the tip, before moving on to define the leg geometry.

Working out leg sweeps...

Reconsidering the fetlock flame approach, I decide using spikes for the flame wisps is simpler and safer than importing the frame helper.

For the body, I'm defining a spine path with four points curving from neck to haunch, paired with varying radii for the sweep to taper the chest and belly naturally, aiming for a total height to the antler tip around 2.35.

With shoulder height near 1.45, this makes the qilin horse-sized, which works. Now I'm adding dorsal spine ridge details by sweeping small gold cone "spikes" along the body's spine line at each sampled point, oriented along the body's facing axis.

For the neck, I'm adding a gold collar torus near the chest with a hanging jade pendant, working out the rotation needed so the torus ring sits perpendicular to the neck's tilt direction rather than flat.

I'm working out where to place the pendant gem relative to the chest cap and collar torus, estimating a position around (0, 1.25, 0.8) so it sits just at the front surface without clipping through the chest geometry.

For the head, I'm placing a glow gem on the forehead using spherical coordinates relative to the skull center, then adding brow ridges, cheek spikes, a lower jaw rod, and tiny teeth cones to give the dragon-like head more structure before moving on to the ground.

I'm checking that the model sits flush with the ground at the hooves, then adding glowing fire-wisp cards at the fetlocks for a qilin-style flame effect. Now I'm settling on the final color palette—pearl body tones, teal scale edges, teal-to-blue mane gradients, gold accents, and amber hooves.

Still writing palette colors...

Now I'm defining the paint helpers—coat and belly shading functions that select colors based on vertical position, using cel-shaded scale textures with soft edge tones for the body.

Working through mane puff lobes with cel-colored spheres, then planning scatter distributions for the mane and tail hair using filtered sampling on the surface. I'm also sketching out beard tufts and whisker sweeps as spike and sweep geometry.

Now I'm drafting the actual leg and haunch geometry: capsules for the thigh and shoulder mass with tapered radii, sweep paths for the body ridge, and a loop generating symmetric front leg points with knee bumps and decreasing radius down to the hoof.

Adding hind leg points, hoof cylinders, and gold fetlock plates...

Triangles look fine, so I'm ready to finalize and write the file.
